description: Compare two builds, then slice the detail. Groups are chosen by cassandra_build, the build each node reports from its own current symlink, so a per-node change of version moves that node between groups on its own. The top section answers whether the candidate build helped, as a number. The lower sections honour the Group by variable and the ad-hoc filters. No host name and no build string is written into this dashboard.

options.content:
Pick a build in **Baseline** and another in **Candidate**. The dropdowns list every `cassandra_build` value present right now, so any split works: one against three, two against two, or one variant at a time. The stat row below is the answer; everything under it is the evidence.

**What the colours mean.** Green means the candidate is better than the baseline; red means worse. The direction is set per metric, so you never have to work it out. Lower is better for latency, GC pause overhead, dropped messages, hints and block I/O, and those turn green on a **negative** delta. Higher is better for throughput, which turns green on a **positive** one. Negative is not always green.

**Before you believe a delta.** A blank delta means the baseline was zero, and a percentage of zero is undefined; panels where that is normal show an absolute difference instead. Check **Per-node request rate spread** first: at 1.00 the nodes of a build are doing equal work, and well above 1.00 the group average is really describing one node. Two nodes on the same build can still disagree by tens of percent, and the per-node panels show it.

**Slicing.** *Ad-hoc filters* applies a label filter to every panel at once. *Group by* re-cuts the Slice and dice section. *Percentile* and *Latency unit* drive every latency panel.

panels.description: Change in read latency at ${percentile}, candidate build against baseline build. Negative is better: the candidate answers reads faster. Set Baseline and Candidate at the top before reading this number.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", cassandra_operation="read"})
  - avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="read"})
) / avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="read"})

panels.title: Read ${percentile}

panels.description: Change in write latency at ${percentile}, candidate build against baseline build. Negative is better: the candidate acknowledges writes faster.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", cassandra_operation="write"})
  - avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="write"})
) / avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="write"})

panels.title: Write ${percentile}

panels.description: Change in coordinator requests per second per node. Positive is better: the candidate serves more work. Read it beside the per-node request rate panel; if the client is not spreading work evenly this number moves without any code change.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}[$__rate_interval])))
  - avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}[$__rate_interval])))
) / avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Change in the share of wall clock time spent in stop-the-world GC pauses. Negative is better. Concurrent cycles are excluded with jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"; without that filter a concurrent collector's cycle time counts as pause time and it looks worse than a stop-the-world collector, which is backwards.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__rate_interval])))
  - avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__rate_interval])))
) / avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: GC pause overhead

panels.description: Change in SSTables touched per read at p99, user keyspaces only. Negative is better: fewer files per query. System keyspaces are excluded here because there are dozens of idle ones and they flatten the number; the sliceable twin further down leaves them in so an ad-hoc keyspace filter can re-scope it. This gauge has no p999, so it stays at p99 and does not follow the Percentile picker.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(cassandra_table_sstables_per_read_p99{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal"})
  - avg(cassandra_table_sstables_per_read_p99{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal"})
) / avg(cassandra_table_sstables_per_read_p99{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal"})

panels.title: SSTables per read p99

panels.description: Change in block device read latency at p99, measured in the kernel by ebpf_exporter. Negative is better. ebpf_exporter does not carry cassandra_build, so the series are narrowed to the nodes of each build with an 'and on (host_name)' join against a Cassandra metric. This family is a real histogram, so histogram_quantile is correct here.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}))))
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))
) / histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))

panels.title: Block I/O read p99

panels.description: One row per node, read from live labels. cassandra_build is derived on each node from the target of the current symlink, so it carries the commit sha and follows a per-node version change on its own. Count the rows for a build to get its node count. The heap ceiling uses max by, never sum: a generational concurrent collector reports the whole heap limit on both its young and its old pool, and a sum would double it on that side only.
panels.title: Nodes, builds and heap ceiling

panels.description: One row per build and collector, read from live labels. The collector name is the clearest single marker of what differs between two JVM configurations: a G1 build shows Young and Old Generation rows, a ZGC build shows Pauses and Cycles rows. Cycles are kept here on purpose so the collector's full shape is visible; every pause measurement elsewhere on this page excludes them.
panels.title: Garbage collector by build

options.content:
### How to use this page

Pick **Baseline** and **Candidate**. Both select over `cassandra_build`, the build each node
reports from its own current symlink, so a node that changes version moves between groups by
itself. Groups are averaged, never summed, so a group of one and a group of five stay comparable.

- **Ad-hoc filters** applies any `label=value` filter to every panel at once.
- **Group by** re-cuts the *Slice and dice* section; each panel names the dimensions it honours.
- **Host** narrows the per-node and slice panels to chosen nodes.
- A red line marks a database restart.
- A blank delta series is not a broken panel: a percentage change needs a non-zero baseline.

panels.description: Highest request rate divided by the lowest, among the nodes of each build. 1.00 means the nodes of that build are doing equal work and an average over them is trustworthy. The further above 1.00, the more the group average is really describing one node. A build running on a single node always reads 1.00. This panel reports the spread and does not claim a cause.
panels.title: Per-node request rate spread (max / min)

panels.description: How many nodes run each build right now. The groups do not have to be the same size; every aggregation on this page averages. A zero means the group selection is empty and every delta above is meaningless.
panels.title: Nodes in each group

panels.description: Read latency at ${percentile} for every node separately, labelled with the build it runs. Two nodes of the same build should sit on top of each other. When they do not, the group average above is describing nodes that disagree, and the aggregate deserves less weight. This panel states the disagreement and offers no explanation for it.

targets.expr: avg by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline|$candidate", host_name=~"$host", cassandra_operation="read"}) / ${latency_unit}

panels.title: Read latency ${percentile} per node (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Coordinator request rate for every node separately, labelled with the build it runs. Use it to see whether the two groups are being asked to do the same amount of work before you read anything into a latency difference.
panels.title: Request rate per node

panels.description: Read latency at ${percentile}, averaged across the nodes of each build. The dashed line on the right axis is the percentage change of the candidate against the baseline; below zero the candidate is faster.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", cassandra_operation="read"})
  - avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="read"})
) / avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="read"})

panels.title: Read latency ${percentile} (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Write latency at ${percentile}, averaged across the nodes of each build. The dashed line on the right axis is the percentage change of the candidate against the baseline; below zero the candidate is faster.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", cassandra_operation="write"})
  - avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="write"})
) / avg(cassandra_client_request_latency_${percentile}_microseconds{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", cassandra_operation="write"})

panels.title: Write latency ${percentile} (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Coordinator requests per second per node, averaged across the nodes of each build. Higher is better. Averaged and never summed, so the two builds stay comparable at any node count.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}[$__rate_interval])))
  - avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}[$__rate_interval])))
) / avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Request throughput per node

panels.description: Messages dropped per second per node. Lower is better. The third series is an absolute difference, not a percentage, because a healthy group drops nothing and a percentage of zero says nothing.
panels.title: Dropped messages

panels.description: Client request errors per second per node across every status. Lower is better. The third series is an absolute difference because a healthy group errors at zero. Add an ad-hoc cassandra_status filter to look at one status alone.
panels.title: Request errors

panels.description: Hints written per second per node, with hints in flight as the two extra series. A node writes a hint when a replica does not answer, so a rise on one side points at a slower or busier peer rather than at the node itself.
panels.title: Hints

panels.description: Share of wall clock time spent in stop-the-world GC pauses. Lower is better. Concurrent cycles are excluded with jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"; without that filter a concurrent collector's cycle time is added to pause time and it looks worse than a stop-the-world collector, which is the wrong answer. The collector each build runs is in the table at the top of the page.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__rate_interval])))
  - avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__rate_interval])))
) / avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: GC pause overhead

panels.description: Heap in use per node, averaged across the nodes of each build, against the heap ceiling. The ceiling uses max by (host_name), never sum: a generational concurrent collector reports the whole heap limit on both its young and its old pool, so a sum doubles the ceiling on that side only.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(sum by (host_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", jvm_memory_type="heap"}))
  - avg(sum by (host_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", jvm_memory_type="heap"}))
) / avg(sum by (host_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", jvm_memory_type="heap"}))

panels.title: Heap used against the ceiling

panels.description: SSTables touched per read at p99, user keyspaces only. Lower is better: compaction is keeping up and a read visits fewer files. This gauge exists only at p50, p99 and max, so it stays at p99 and does not follow the Percentile picker.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    avg(cassandra_table_sstables_per_read_p99{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate", keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal"})
  - avg(cassandra_table_sstables_per_read_p99{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal"})
) / avg(cassandra_table_sstables_per_read_p99{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline", keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal"})

panels.title: SSTables per read p99

panels.description: Compaction tasks waiting per node. Lower is better. The third series is an absolute difference, not a percentage, because a healthy backlog is zero.
panels.title: Compaction backlog

panels.description: Compactions finished per second per node. Higher is better while the backlog panel is not empty: the node clears work faster. Storage and I/O changes act here first.
panels.title: Compaction completion rate

panels.description: Live data on disk per node. The two builds should track each other. A lasting gap means one side holds data the other has already compacted away, or that a node joined the ring later and carries less. Either way it makes a latency comparison suspect, because the two sides are no longer reading the same shape of data.
panels.title: Storage load per node

panels.description: Block device read latency at p99, measured in the kernel by ebpf_exporter. Lower is better. ebpf_exporter does not carry cassandra_build, so each series is narrowed to the nodes of one build with an 'and on (host_name)' join against a Cassandra metric. This family is a real histogram, so histogram_quantile is correct here, unlike the Cassandra latency gauges.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}))))

100 * (
    histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}))))
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))
) / histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))

panels.title: Block I/O read latency p99

panels.description: Page cache work per second per node, from ebpf_exporter, narrowed to the nodes of each build with an 'and on (host_name)' join. A build that reads around the page cache does less of this. Four series rather than a delta line, because the split between cache writes and dirty pages is the point and one percentage would hide it.

targets.expr: avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_page_cache_ops_total{operation="cache_writes"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))

avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_page_cache_ops_total{operation="cache_writes"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}))))

avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_page_cache_ops_total{operation="page_mark_dirties"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$baseline"}))))

avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(ebpf_exporter_page_cache_ops_total{operation="page_mark_dirties"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (host_name) (count by (host_name) (cassandra_client_request_count_total{job="cassandra", cassandra_build=~"$candidate"}))))

panels.title: Page cache activity

panels.description: Client latency at ${percentile}, cut by ${groupby}, across every node the Host picker allows. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster and cassandra_operation. Range slice requests are left out because they idle at zero in most tests and a zero series drags any average that mixes operations. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Latency ${percentile} by ${groupby} (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Coordinator request rate cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster and cassandra_operation. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Request rate by ${groupby}

panels.description: Client request errors cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster, cassandra_operation and cassandra_status. Group by cassandra_status to separate unavailable from timeout from failure. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Request errors by ${groupby}

panels.description: Dropped messages cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster and message_type. Group by message_type to see which verb is being shed. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Dropped messages by ${groupby}

panels.description: Thread pool queue depth cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster, pool and pool_path. Group by pool to find which stage is backing up; a rising queue here is the cause of the symptoms above. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Thread pool pending by ${groupby}

panels.description: Rate at which thread pool tasks are blocked, cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster, pool and pool_path. Anything above zero means a caller is being made to wait, which is real backpressure rather than a queue that is merely deep. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Thread pool blocked rate by ${groupby}

panels.description: SSTables touched per read at p99, cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster, keyspace and table. No keyspace is excluded here, so an ad-hoc keyspace or table filter can scope it to whatever the test writes. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: SSTables per read p99 by ${groupby}

panels.description: Live bytes on disk cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster, keyspace and table. Group by table to see which table is actually growing. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Live disk space by ${groupby}

panels.description: Stop-the-world GC pause overhead cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster and jvm_gc_name. Concurrent cycles are excluded, so grouping by jvm_gc_name shows the pause phases only; the table at the top of the page keeps the cycles in. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: GC pause overhead by ${groupby}

panels.description: Heap in use cut by ${groupby}. Honours cassandra_build, host_name, cluster and jvm_memory_pool_name. Group by jvm_memory_pool_name to see the shape of the heap, which is where two collectors differ most. Only the ten largest series are drawn.
panels.title: Heap used by ${groupby}

list.description: The reference build. Read from the cassandra_build label, which each node derives from the target of its own current symlink, so it carries the commit sha and follows a per-node version change.
list.label: Baseline
list.name: baseline

list.description: The build under test. The two groups do not have to hold the same number of nodes; every panel averages rather than sums.
list.label: Candidate
list.name: candidate

list.description: Drill-down. Narrows the per-node panels and the whole Slice and dice section to chosen nodes. Leave it on All for the normal build against build view.
list.label: Host
list.name: host

list.description: Which pre-aggregated latency gauge to read. The gauges are computed per node, so a group is averaged and never summed.
list.label: Percentile
list.name: percentile

list.description: Display unit for latency. The metric is emitted in microseconds, so the value is the divisor: milliseconds divides by 1000, microseconds divides by 1.
list.label: Latency unit
list.name: latency_unit

list.description: Dimension for every panel in the Slice and dice section. Defaults to cassandra_build, so the section compares what the nodes are running rather than what they are called. Not every metric carries every label; each panel names the ones it honours, and a label the metric does not carry collapses that panel to one unlabelled series.
list.label: Group by
